title: Formal MSC quad-cells (max-saddle-min-saddle topology)
description:
PATCH-24 ascending-manifold cells aren't quads — each cell can have any number of saddles on its boundary. For Coons-fittable patches (the project's end goal), cells need exactly 4 corners and 4 sides forming the canonical MSC 2-cell topology: alternating max → saddle → min → saddle → max around each cell.

This is the formal Morse-Smale complex 2-cell construction (Edelsbrunner-Harer). On a 2-manifold with persistence-simplified critical points, every cell of the MSC IS a quad. We just haven't built that representation — we have ascending manifolds, which are coarser.

Algorithm:
1. From PATCH-26's MSC result + arcs, build the arc-graph topology (which arcs share endpoints, which arcs lie on cell boundaries).
2. For each maximum, walk its incident arcs CCW. Each adjacent pair of arcs (out to one saddle, then over to a min via descending arc, then back via another descending arc, then up to another saddle, then up the next ascending arc) defines one quad cell.
3. Output: List<Cell> where each Cell has 4 corner critical-point IDs (max, sad1, min, sad2), 4 sides (each a vertex polyline along an arc), and one interior face-set.

Reference: Edelsbrunner-Harer "Computational Topology" Ch. VII; Gyulassy practical MSC paper.

Likely depends on PATCH-28 (boundary snap) so the arcs we walk are clean.

Acceptance: each MSC cell on the skull has exactly 4 corners; cells are addressable as {maxId, sad1Id, minId, sad2Id}; PatchDecomposition output emits cells with their 4 ordered side polylines, ready for Coons-cage Bezier fitting.

**v1 results 2026-04-25** (commits in MscQuadCells.java, Patch.cornerVertices, SharedBoundaryRegistry explicit-corners path): wedge-by-tangent-angle face assignment was wrong. 71% of faces fell back to nearest-quad-Euclidean, 1272 saddle pairs missing common min, Coons p95 doubled (0.180 → 0.443). Quads built (580) but face boundaries are jagged Voronoi-in-3D, not formal MSC cells.

**v2 design (canonical Edelsbrunner / Gyulassy / DisPerSE / TTK approach):** every face's quad cell is the *intersection* of its ascending manifold (max) and descending manifold (min). Algorithm:
  1. ascendingManifold gives per-face max id (already exists).
  2. NEW descendingManifold gives per-face min id (parallel walk on smoothed scalar, downhill).
  3. Quad set = unique (max, min) pairs seen across faces.
  4. For each (M, M') pair: 2 saddles connect them in arc graph (theorem); these are the quad's 2 saddle corners.
  5. PatchDecomposition: facePatchId = quad index of face's (max, min) pair.

Replaces v1 steps B (wedge enumeration with common-min lookup) and C (wedge-by-angle face assignment) entirely. Step A's CCW ordering retained as a per-quad consistency assertion (expect 2 saddles, log degenerate cases).

Future work flagged: Robins-Wood-Sheppard discrete gradient field (TTK uses it; ~5000 LOC) would improve visual arc quality but isn't required for label correctness. Defer.

**References (formal MSC literature):**
- Computing 2D Morse-Smale Complexes (parallel paper, IISc): https://vgl.csa.iisc.ac.in/pdf/pub/mscomplex_parallel.pdf
- Edelsbrunner et al., MSC for Piecewise Linear 3-Manifolds: https://pub.ista.ac.at/~edels/Papers/2003-08-MorseSmaleComplexes3D.pdf
- Gyulassy et al., A Practical Approach to MSC Computation: https://www.cs.jhu.edu/~misha/ReadingSeminar/Papers/Gyulassy08.pdf
- Robins-Wood-Sheppard, Discrete Morse Complexes from Grayscale Images: https://people.physics.anu.edu.au/~vbr110/papers/RWS_TPAMI.pdf
- Revisiting Accurate Geometry for Morse-Smale Complexes (arxiv 2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05532v1
- DisPerSE: General Concepts of Morse Theory: https://www.iap.fr/useriap/sousbie/web/html/index1f6e.html?post%2Fgeneral-concepts=
- Conforming Morse-Smale Complexes (Gyulassy 2014): https://julien-tierny.github.io/stuff/papers/gyulassy_vis14.pdf
- Topology ToolKit (TTK) — open source MSC implementation: https://github.com/topology-tool-kit/ttk
definition-of-done:
1. New MscQuadCells.java assembles formal 2-cells from the MSC arc graph.
2. Each cell has exactly 4 corners and 4 ordered side polylines.
3. Patch records carry the corner/side metadata so a downstream Coons-fit consumer can use it directly.
4. Skull decomposition: every cell is 4-sided; no n-gons except where arc graph has degeneracies that simplify with higher persistence.
testing-plan:
1. VerifyMsDecomposer headless asserts every cell has 4 corners.
2. Render flat patches: cells visibly tile as quads on the skull.
3. Wire to Coons-fit (PATCH-16) and confirm error stats are reasonable for a 4-sided cell layout.
